title: Beyond representational alignment with brain-guided language models for robust reasoning
methods: neural predictivity with explainable-variance noise ceiling
joint model-brain representation structure for steering-direction induction
data_sources: Human Connectome Project (WU-Minn) relational-processing task fMRI
ten open-weight LLMs (Qwen2/Qwen3, Llama 2/3, Mistral, Phi-4-mini, Gemma 2 families cited)
out-of-distribution deductive reasoning test suite (Saparov et al., NeurIPS 2023)
Brain-guided_LLM code and generated data (GitHub + Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19536182)

data_scope.primary_fmri: OpenNeuro ds003076, task-based fMRI of deductive reasoning; dataset descriptor (Lytle, Prado & Booth, Data Brief 33:106405, 2020) documents school-aged children
data_scope.participant_counts: not stated in the openly accessible text (Abstract + Data availability); article is Hybrid Access and Methods are paywalled
data_scope.headline_effect: up to 13% absolute accuracy gain; gains orthogonal to language-only supervision; transfer across reasoning types
data_scope.supplementary: Sections 1-13, Figs. 1-14, Table 1, plus Peer Review file

core_conclusion: LLM internal representations are partially aligned with task-evoked fMRI activity in human reasoning-related regions - explaining a substantial fraction of the explainable variance at the aggregate level but much less within specific reasoning types, evidencing both alignment and divergence. Going beyond measurement, steering model representations along directions induced by the joint structure of model and brain representations - applied as inference-time intervention or as fine-tuning - directly improves deductive reasoning across ten LLMs (1.5B-72B), with up to 13% absolute accuracy gain that is orthogonal to language-only supervision and transfers across reasoning types.
why_it_matters: Converts brain-model alignment from a descriptive scoreboard into a causal training signal; targets reasoning rather than the language network, exploiting the dissociability of language and thought in the human brain; shows that a few hours of public fMRI can improve models up to 72B parameters with gains that stack on top of text supervision, implying task-evoked neural data carries information text corpora do not; reports the aggregate-vs-within-type divergence honestly; releases code, generated data and figure-level source data.
why_nature: Genuine cross-disciplinary synthesis (cognitive neuroscience x learning algorithms x computational science, the journal's own subject tags); advances the field's key open problem from correlation to guidance rather than adding another alignment benchmark; demonstrated at scale across ten models and two intervention regimes with cross-type transfer; engages directly with the high-profile 'understanding vs pattern-matching' debate; offers a programme other labs can adopt; open code, open data and published peer-review reports (reviewer Martin Schrimpf, a founder of the Brain-Score paradigm it extends).
added_value_to_my_research: Brain-guided steering of spatial reasoning -> a cognitive-map-primed GeoAI agent for catchment and route inference
Ceiling-normalized explainable-variance decomposition -> honest evaluation metric for MGWR/ML spatial prediction
Stratify-the-supervision-source audit -> representativeness and equity protocol for cohort-trained health-access models
Joint-structure injection of a scarce exogenous modality -> fine-tuning geospatial foundation models with tiny GPS/mobile-phone/health-utilization signals
Locality-guaranteed intervention plus FAIR release -> deployment audit protocol for LLM agents in urban and public-health policy
